quests.title: Four a Week, All of Them Light
quests.description:
Caravan-Master Bohl has been complaining about the ramp for three years because the ramp is safe to complain about.

The actual problem is on his tally sheet. Four caravans a week come up and every one of them arrives lighter than it left, by an amount that is too consistent to be theft and too large to be spillage. Somebody is taking a cut, in the open, and the drivers have stopped mentioning it.
quests.accept_text:
The road east runs between the Sisters and there is a gap you have to go through. That is where it happens.

Go and stand in that gap and see what it costs. Bring me their tally slips - they write it down, which is the part I cannot get past. They are not robbing us. They are invoicing us.
quests.turn_in_text:
Itemised. Dated. In a hand better than my clerk's.

I wanted to be angry about this and now I have to go and think about something else instead.

quests.title: One Road In
quests.description:
Sentry Palla says the single ramp is a better defence than Thunder Bluff ever had, and she means it, and she also knows exactly what it means to say it.

For the last two weeks something has been working the bottom of it after dark. Not attacking. Testing - coming up far enough to be seen and then going back down, every night, a little further each time.
quests.accept_text:
Hyena. I am nearly sure it is hyena, and nearly sure is why I am sending somebody instead of going myself.

Work the bottom of the ramp and the scrub either side of it, and go out as far as the first bend of the Windward Road. If something is teaching them that this ramp is worth walking up, I want to know whether it is a pack or a person.
quests.turn_in_text:
A pack. Good.

I would rather it were hunger than somebody's idea. Hunger I can post a sentry against.

quests.title: What the Kodo Will Not Do
quests.description:
Stablemaster Reth keeps every four-legged animal in the city on the Landing, because kodo will not cross a rope bridge and worked that out faster than the tauren did.

Which means the pens are up here and the feed is down there, and twice a season somebody has to go and cut it. It is nobody's favourite week.
quests.accept_text:
There is grass in the wash beds that is worth cutting - the only green on the whole floor, and it is green because that is where the year's water went.

Take a blade down and bring back what you can carry. Watch for scorpid in the shade of the cut banks. They are in there because it is cool and they will not move for you.
quests.turn_in_text:
Smells like the plain. It does not taste like the plain and the kodo know, but they eat it.

Everything up here is a version of something we used to have.

quests.title: They Came Down and They Cannot Go Up
quests.description:
Skywatcher Rell can see the dark line of the aspen along the north on a clear day, and three years ago that line was sky.

Things have been coming down it. Elk, mostly - they came off the mountain into what looked like open country, walked south until the timber ran out, and found red hardpan and forty degrees. They cannot find the pass again. They are standing on the Seam in the heat of the day waiting for a weather that is not coming.
quests.accept_text:
I am not asking you to cull them and I would not call it that.

They are going down on their feet out there and the cats came after them and are doing no better. Go and finish what the sun has started, both of them, and do it close enough that it is quick. That is the whole task and I am sorry it is one.
quests.turn_in_text:
You will have seen the ribs on them.

We came down a pass too. The difference is that we knew what we were walking into and we still argue about whether that was better.

quests.title: The Wrong Climate
quests.description:
Healer Ilna Softstep treats falls, mostly, and off ladders rather than off edges. Lately she has been treating something else: drivers coming up the ramp with heat sickness in a season they have worked their whole lives.

She thinks the floor is getting hotter. She would like to be wrong, and she has worked out a way to find out that does not depend on her being right.
quests.accept_text:
Bring me marrow from the elk dying on the Seam and a scrape of the ground they are dying on.

An animal that starves and an animal that cooks do not leave the same marrow. If it is the heat, I will know, and I will have to go and tell Namka that the floor is changing under a city that cannot move.
quests.turn_in_text:
Heat. Not hunger.

I wanted hunger. Hunger would have meant they were simply in the wrong place, and this means the place is going wrong.

quests.title: Harpies Weave
quests.description:
Bowyer Tesh builds better bows than her mother did and has never stopped being annoyed about why.

She has been looking at harpy nest-work through a glass from the Windward top for a season. It is woven. Laid in courses, like thatch, with a turn at the end of each course that she cannot do and cannot stop thinking about.
quests.accept_text:
Bring me the weave. Not a handful of feathers - a piece with the courses still in it, big enough that I can see where the turn goes.

And yes, you will have to kill them to get it, and no, I have not found a way around that, and I have thought about it more than you have.
quests.turn_in_text:
There. That is a bowyer's knot or near enough, and it is being tied by something everyone in this city calls an animal.

I am not going to say that out loud yet. I would like to be sure first, which is more courtesy than most of them get.

quests.title: Nothing Walks Up the Anvil
quests.description:
Lookout Sima has the highest standing ground in Thousand Needles and a list of the four mesas nobody has ever been on top of. The Anvil is the nearest of them.

For eleven nights there has been a light up there. Not a fire - a fire sits still. This moves along the rim and goes out and comes back, and she has counted the pattern and the pattern does not repeat.
quests.accept_text:
Get round the base of it and as high as the scree will take you. I am not asking you to climb the unclimbable, I am asking you to get close enough to see what is making that light.

The rooktenders come down to hunt at dusk. If you can take a few on the way it will be a quieter approach, and I will not pretend that is not also useful to me.
quests.turn_in_text:
Carried. Something is carrying it along the rim and putting it down.

Then they signal. Then that is a thing they do, and I have been writing them up as weather for three years.

quests.title: An Itemised Document
quests.description:
Tally-Clerk Nessa writes down everything that crosses this top, and she will tell you it is not suspicion - it is that the tauren lost a city once without a list of what was in it.

Bohl has brought her four Galak tally slips and she has not slept properly since. They are better kept than hers. Dated, carried forward, with a running balance and a column she cannot identify.
quests.accept_text:
I need more of it. Not slips - leaves out of the book the slips come from, and you will find those on whoever is senior in a toll party.

I want to know what that fourth column is. If they are keeping a balance against us then they think we owe them something specific, and I would like to know what before the council decides for me.
quests.turn_in_text:
It is a running total. Against the road.

They are not charging us to pass. They are charging us for the road, and they have been maintaining the road, and there is a column for that too.

quests.title: At the Foot of the Ramp
quests.description:
Warden Hesk Stonefoot watches everything that comes up the ramp because everything that reaches this city comes up it. He is not a nervous man and he has been nervous for a month.

Galak outriders have started standing at the bottom. Not blocking it. Standing at it, in daylight, in numbers, where the whole Landing can look down and count them.
quests.accept_text:
The Khan's Chosen are the ones with the standard. Where they stand, the rest form up, and they have been forming up closer each week.

Go down and make the ground in front of that ramp expensive. I am not asking for a war. I am asking them to do their standing somewhere I cannot see it from my own gate.
quests.turn_in_text:
They have moved back. Half a mile, and in good order, which I notice.

Nobody routed. They decided. That is worse and I am going to say so to the council whether they want it or not.

quests.title: What the Quartermaster Wants Less Of
quests.description:
Quartermaster Bren Hollowhorn prices everything by the back that carried it up the ramp, and lately every back is costing more because of what is standing at the bottom.

She is not interested in the philosophy. She has a column that says what the escort costs and she would like it to be a smaller number by the end of the season.
quests.accept_text:
The wind-readers are the ones that make a toll party work. They sit high, they see the dust of a caravan an hour out, and the riders are formed up and waiting before the drivers know they are seen.

Take the readers out and the riders are guessing. Take enough of them and my escort column halves. That is the whole of my reasoning and I am not going to dress it up.
quests.turn_in_text:
Down a third already. I will take a third.

You will hear Namka say we should be talking to them. She is probably right. She is also not the one buying rope.

quests.title: Namka Sends a Word
quests.description:
High Elder Namka Windhollow built this city and cannot get used to having built something again. She has listened to the warden, the quartermaster and the clerk, and she has read the fourth column in the Galak ledger, and she has reached a conclusion the council will hate.

The Galak are not raiding Freewind. They are charging it for a road they maintain, and nobody on either side has ever once said so out loud.

objectives.label: Put Namka's word in the hand of a Galak toll party

quests.accept_text:
This goes to the Sisters, to whoever is standing in that gap, and it goes into a hand - not stuck in the ground, not left on a stone.

They will not kill you for carrying it. They have never killed a driver who paid and they have never killed one who could not. Walk up with it held where they can see it and do not draw anything, and if that frightens you then you have understood the task.
quests.turn_in_text:
Taken. Read, in front of you, and taken.

Then we are talking. Three years and a dead road and a city in the air, and all it needed was somebody willing to walk up holding a piece of paper. I will be a long time forgiving myself for the three years.

quests.title: Everything Comes Up the Ramp
quests.description:
Potter Hesha will tell you that if you ever want to understand this city, you should stand at the bottom of the ramp for a day. Her clay comes up it in sacks, from a pit four days west, and every pot in Freewind is priced accordingly.

There is clay in the salt pans east of here, two days closer. Everyone has told her it will not fire. Nobody has tried it.
quests.accept_text:
Dig me seven good sacks off the pans at Saltwatch. Below the crust - the crust is salt and salt is what ruins a pot. Under it there is grey clay and I want to see it.

The things that live out on those pans are made of the same salt. Do not let them get close enough to put it on you.
quests.turn_in_text:
It fires. Pale, and it rings higher than the western clay, and it is going to crack in the cold if the cold ever comes.

Two days closer. Two days closer is a different city.

quests.title: Older Than Any of This
quests.description:
Spirit-Walker Enu has spent three years looking for the dead of Thunder Bluff and not finding them, and has found the only comfort available in the not-finding.

He has been out to Dryhollow twice. He wants it understood, by somebody who will carry it back and repeat it, that what is wrong with Dryhollow is not the Integration's doing. It was wrong before. It will be wrong after. Not everything broken in this world was broken by Earth arriving.
quests.accept_text:
Go out to the hollow and stand in the middle of it for as long as you can manage, and then come back and tell me what you felt.

The basilisks will not let you stand anywhere for long, so thin them first. They are old. They are the oldest thing on this map and they were doing this when the needles were still being cut by water.
quests.turn_in_text:
Nothing. You felt nothing, and that is the answer.

Everywhere the Integration touched feels like a held breath. Dryhollow feels like a room nobody has been in. It is simply old, and I needed one thing in this country to be simply old.

quests.title: The Pan You Can See Yourself In
quests.description:
Relic-Keeper Dun can tell you whether a thing came up out of the mesas or down off the mountain. He cannot always tell you what either one is, and he is honest about the gap, which is rarer in his trade than it should be.

A salt crew came back from the far side of Dryhollow talking about a pan fused to glass. A sheet of it, flat, with the sky in it. They would not go nearer and they would not go back.
quests.accept_text:
Go and look at it and bring me pieces off the edge.

I will tell you what the crew told me, which is that something lives out there and that it is still making the glass. Look at the pan, take your pieces off the rim of it, and do not go to the middle to find out what is standing in the middle. Nothing I want is worth that.
quests.turn_in_text:
Fused all the way through. Not glazed - fused, like it went through a kiln the size of the hollow.

I am going to put this on the shelf and label it honestly: came up out of the mesas, cause unknown, do not go to the middle.

quests.title: Pale Wood, Wrong Wood
quests.description:
Timberwright Gohn has stopped finding it strange that every plank in this city came off a mountain that was not here three years ago, and he has been told that is the strange part.

The bridges want relaying before the windy season. Three spans, and the rope gets all the attention because rope is frightening and decking is not, which is exactly backwards.
quests.accept_text:
Mill me six lengths and bring four sound bolts up from the stacks to replace what you use.

Aspen takes a bend and holds it, which is why the bowyer is insufferable lately, and it is why a deck board on a rope span wants to be aspen and not anything that grew down here. Nothing that grew down here bends. It just goes.
quests.turn_in_text:
Good work and dull work, and dull work is what a bridge is made of.

When somebody walks across that span and thinks about the rope, they are thinking about the wrong thing, and that is the compliment.

quests.title: Where the Water Goes
quests.description:
Warehouse-Keeper Dral knows where everything that came up the ramp this season is, and will tell you to stop asking about anything that did not.

What he cannot account for is water. Thousand Needles floods once a year, hard, and then is dry for twelve months. That much water does not evaporate. It goes somewhere, and whatever it goes into has been filling and emptying since before anyone here was born.
quests.accept_text:
At the foot of Broadback there is a wash that runs in and does not run out. I want you to go and stand at the mouth of it and look down.

The kodo shelter in the mouth of it in the heat and they will not like you there. Clear enough of them that you can get a proper look, and then come back and tell me how far down you could see before it stopped being down.
quests.turn_in_text:
No bottom to it that you could see. A year's water, every year, into a hole with no bottom.

I have a column in my book for things that go out and do not come back. I am going to need a bigger column.

quests.title: They Were People
quests.description:
The Rememberer holds the names of everyone who was in Thunder Bluff when the ground took the city, in order, and says them through once a season. It takes most of a night and he is not going to stop.

Dral has told him what is down the hole at Broadback. There are things walking in it with salt set hard over them, and they have hands, and somebody somewhere has a list with their names on it.
quests.accept_text:
I am not asking you to put them down out of mercy. You can decide that for yourself and I would not argue with either answer.

I am asking you to bring back anything they are carrying that was made rather than grown. A stick with notches. A ring. A tally. Something that says a person kept it, so that I can say what they were before the water, and not only that they drowned.
quests.turn_in_text:
Tally sticks. Salt crews, then - the ones that work the pans east and come back through the washes in the wet month.

Five of them. That is five names I can find, and finding five names is the only work I have ever been good at.

quests.title: It Feeds Once
quests.description:
Dral has stopped keeping a column for the hole at Broadback and started keeping a page.

The salt crews that come back through the washes have a story they tell each other and not outsiders: that there is something in the standing water at the bottom that does not eat all year. It waits for the flood. When the cave fills, everything in it drowns at once, and the thing in the sump has its one meal and then waits another year.
quests.accept_text:
The flood is four months out, which means everything down there is alive and the thing in the sump is as hungry as it ever gets.

The water never drains out of the lowest bay. Go to it. Whatever is in there has no eyes and has never needed any, and three of my drivers have told me the same thing about how it finds you, which is that it waits until you move.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then the crews were right and I have been filing their story under rumour for two years.

There is a page in my book for that too. I am going to go and change it, and I am going to make a note about who told me first.

quests.title: The Road Is Open
quests.description:
Namka has a thing she has not had in three years, which is a road and somebody to talk to at both ends of it.

The Galak will let a caravan through and have put a price on it that is written down. The hole under Broadback has had the thing at the bottom of it taken out of it. There is nothing left between Camp Taurajo and this city except distance, and distance is a problem the tauren have solved before.

objectives.label: Carry the accord to Wrangler Tull at Camp Taurajo

quests.accept_text:
Take this north. All of it - the terms, the toll, the schedule, and the Galak's own hand at the bottom of it, which took longer to get than any of the rest.

Tull asked whether kodo could go down. Tell him yes. Tell him it costs, tell him who it costs, and tell him we are paying it and that we think the price is fair, and watch his face while you say that last part.
quests.turn_in_text:
Signed by a centaur. There is a centaur's mark on a tauren document and somebody expects me to read it out at the corral gate.

I drove that road for twenty years and I never once paid a toll on it. I also never once had to ask who kept it up. Fine. Fine, lass. We will pay.
